text:
tomi: FYI canary p95 jumped ~2.1x on kernel selector after the nightly merge. Seeing it across a few model families.

lina: ugh, which merge? any obvious change?

samir: looks like the merge that tweaked kernel-priority scoring landed 1801200000 (PR #8741).

kevin: I ran the perf harness locally (small repro) and saw the same p95 delta when the new heuristic is enabled. Repro steps: `./perf/run_workload.sh --profile kernel --model gpt-small --seq 1024 --concurrency 16`

qa-bot: CI: post-merge perf check failed for nightly/variant-x (p95 2100ms -> 4400ms). Link: https://ci.internal/perf/18012345

samir: OK let's bisect the commit range quickly. Suggest `git bisect start --first-parent HEAD 1801195000 && git bisect run ./infra/ci/scripts/perf-bisect.sh` (the script returns non-zero if p95>1.5x baseline).

lina: before we go full bisect, note KV cache warmup can hide regressions. When running locally toggle `KV_CACHE_WARMUP=0` to force cold cache to replicate canary conditions. I saw an interaction where kernel choice increased cache churn.

kevin: good catch. With KV_CACHE_WARMUP=0 I repro faster and get consistent failures. Also attached a tiny profile (top hotspots):

```
# perf top snapshot
  22.3%  runtime.so  kernel_selector::score_candidates
  18.1%  runtime.so  kv_cache::evict_and_insert
  12.5%  libcuda.so  cuLaunchKernel
```

samir: that points to the scorer allocating/iterating more, causing evictions. I suspect the new scoring loop does an O(n^2) pass for rare shapes. I will run `git bisect` with the cache off and the perf script.

eng-sre: heads up — this is blocking the canary rollout. If bisect finds the offending commit, we should prepare an emergency revert patch to unblock traffic.

samir: halfway through bisect now. Preliminary candidate: commit 1801204002 changes kernel priority filter and adds a fallback loop (looks suspicious).

tomi: can someone locally build that commit and run the repro with `KV_CACHE_WARMUP=0`? If it reproduces, we prep revert.

kevin: built and tested commit 1801204002 — repro confirmed. p95 matches the canary. I pushed a quick patch to disable the fallback loop (branch `hotfix/disable-fallback-8741`) and perf returns to baseline.

lina: are there any downstream implications of disabling fallback? Might affect rare sequences but better than outage. We should write a unit/regression test to guard against the O(n^2) path.

samir: agreed. I'll open a PR to revert the heuristic change (or at least gate it behind a flag) and add perf tests. PR draft: #8750.

eng-sre: scheduling an emergency rollback for the nightly canary to unblock. Deployment window in 10m. @deploy-bot will post status.

ci-bot: rollback job queued: rollback/nightly-180123 -> started.

tomi: thanks all. Follow-up actions: (1) land hotfix PR to revert/gate (samir), (2) add regression perf test and KV-cache cold-run to CI (lina), (3) postmortem + checklist for kernel-selector changes (me).

kevin: I'll also add an extra smoke that runs KV_CACHE_WARMUP=0 in our canary pipeline so we catch this earlier.

lina: adding note: when changing kernel selection logic, run `perf/ci/kv_cold.sh` locally and in pre-merge CI.

tomi: closing loop — once rollback finishes, let's validate canary and then land the hotfix behind a feature flag with telemetry. :thumbsup:
